requirements.requirement: Containerized web application runs as the unprivileged appsvc account (rootless)
requirements.summary: appsvc (uid 1000, non-root) was created and used to pull and run the nginx:alpine container rootlessly via podman/Quadlet. Post-reboot process inspection confirms the nginx master process (pid 915) is owned by appsvc, not root, demonstrating the running container is truly unprivileged.

Quadlet unit publishes PublishPort=8080:80; podman ps shows 0.0.0.0:8080->80/tcp; curl to the node on 8080 returns HTTP 200 both before and after a full reboot; the after-executor lifecycle snapshot independently confirms a listening socket on *:8080 owned by the pasta rootless network helper.

requirements.requirement: Service starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
requirements.summary: Full bounded reboot transition was captured, not just configuration: healthy baseline (linger enabled, generator-created default.target.wants symlink, webapp active, HTTP 200, boot_id 03408ac4...) -> reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect -> node unreachable during restart -> new boot_id cbea0e05... confirming an actual reboot -> recovered state showing no interactive login session for appsvc (loginctl shows only the lingering user-manager entry, session count reduced from 2 to 1 and no tty/pts session), user@1000.service active, webapp.service active, container auto-started, HTTP 200, and nginx process owned by appsvc.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: the app runs rootless under appsvc, serves on port 8080, and a genuine bounded reboot test (distinct pre/post boot IDs, disconnect during restart, and full post-reboot recovery of service, container, HTTP response, and process ownership) confirms it starts at boot without an active appsvc login session. The independent lifecycle snapshots corroborate the boot-identity change and the new listening socket on 8080. Hygiene is good overall; the only ding is leftover diagnostic residue (/tmp/rhkey.gpg and dnf/pull logs) from a GPG troubleshooting detour that turned out unnecessary once the plain retry succeeded.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was captured for node1 (the only managed node), so no additional restart cycles were available to further corroborate stability of the boot autostart mechanism.
The before_prepare and after_prepare snapshots are identical (prepare was disabled), so the prepare-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the before/after-executor comparison.

Systemd `--user enable` reported the unit as generated/transient, which is expected for Quadlet-generated units; boot autostart instead relies on the generator's default.target.wants symlink, confirmed present and functioning across the observed reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to the task: user/linger creation, podman install, image pull, Quadlet unit creation, firewalld port opening, and the reboot itself. One troubleshooting excursion was not clearly load-bearing: after the first podman install attempt failed on a transient dnf GPG-parsing error (cmd-b36cafac70154729), the executor ran `gpg --dearmor` on the RHEL release key into /tmp/rhkey.gpg (cmd-da30be3b205249ea) as a diagnostic experiment; the subsequent successful install (cmd-0ceb776b90b04a8f) used the normal dnf/GPG path and did not depend on that dearmored key, so the mutation appears unnecessary. Its residue (/tmp/rhkey.gpg) and the diagnostic dnf logs (/tmp/dnf_install.log, /tmp/dnf_install2.log, /tmp/pull.log) are confirmed still present in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot rather than cleaned up. This is low-risk, bounded, and non-destructive (no security weakening, no service disruption), but it is retained residue from a failed troubleshooting path rather than fully restored.
